best_for: IT admins and cautious users who want Firefox on a slow, predictable track, with security fixes but no feature changes between yearly upgrades.
description:
Firefox ESR, short for Extended Support Release, is the edition of Firefox that Mozilla builds for organizations: businesses, schools and public offices that roll out one browser to many computers. It is the same open source browser, held on a long-lived branch so an IT team can plan around it.

Admins can set enterprise policies to lock down how the browser behaves, enforce security settings, preset features or switch some of them off. Mozilla publishes the policy templates on GitHub and a full policy reference in its Firefox admin docs. You can push Firefox ESR to your fleet with the tools you already use, such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf or another device management system.

points.title: Fixes now, features once a year
points.text: ESR gets a point release about every two weeks, paired with regular Firefox releases, carrying security fixes. New features arrive in bulk when a new ESR branch starts, roughly once a year. The current branch is 153.

points.title: Know your end dates
points.text: Mozilla's release calendar ends ESR 153 on September 21, 2027, when updates move to ESR 175. ESR 175 starts on June 29, 2027, which leaves an overlap to test before you switch.

points.title: 153 needs Windows 10 or macOS 10.15
points.text: ESR 153 runs on Windows 10 or newer and macOS 10.15 or newer. Machines on Windows 7 to 8.1 or macOS 10.12 to 10.14 stay on ESR 115, which Mozilla's calendar ends on April 6, 2027.

points.title: Free, with paid support available
points.text: The browser is free under the Mozilla Public License 2.0. Mozilla sells a paid support plan for companies that make Firefox their standard browser, priced through sales.

points.title: Downgrades on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 101 versions, with machine-wide installers for x86, x64 and Arm64. macOS lists only the current universal build, so an older Mac release needs another source.
